name: application-discount-code-field
title: Discount Code Field
description: Promo code input with an Apply action that transitions to a real applied (savings, removable) or invalid (inline error) state.
useWhen: Letting users enter a promo/coupon code during checkout and see clear confirmation of what it did.
You need distinct visual states for entering, applying, succeeding, and failing a code — not just a plain text input.
Pairing with `checkout-order-summary`, which shows the resulting discount line and updated total.
avoidWhen: You need a general-purpose copyable value display (API keys, invite links) — use `copy-field` instead, which is built for that direction (copying out, not validating in).
Discounts apply automatically without a user-entered code — this pattern implies manual entry and validation.
Only one code can ever be valid and there's no failure mode to design for — a plain input may be sufficient.
responsiveBehavior: Input and button share a flex row that keeps the button a fixed width while the input shrinks; stacks acceptably at narrow widths without additional overrides.
accessibility: The invalid state sets aria-invalid on the input and aria-describedby pointing at the error message, which carries role="alert" so it's announced immediately.
The applied state's remove button has an aria-label naming the specific code, not a generic "Remove".
Success and error feedback are both communicated via text, not color alone (a savings amount sentence, an explicit error sentence).
The field has an associated <label>, not just a placeholder, so its purpose persists after text is entered.

variants.title: Discount Code Field
variants.description: Three states: an empty default field, an applied code with a savings chip, and an invalid code with an inline error.
accessibility: State transitions (idle → applied/invalid) are driven by a real typed state machine, not just class toggles on static markup.

variants.title: Discount Code Field (Dark)
variants.description: Discount code field adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Applied and invalid state colors are tuned to meet WCAG AA contrast against the dark surface.
